c: 108 Responsive Prayers creates ofuda amulets in a spiral vertically around the user, with the ofuda amulets rotating in the same direction as the user. When the weapon fires, after a short delay, it will create explosions centered on these amulets, displaying the characters "不", "動", "明", and "王", (a Buddhist Bodhisattva), dealing damage to enemies hit as the explosions continue down the screen.
The damage of the above explosions is increased by +1% for every 1% difference in
, maxing out at a damage increase of 11x at a difference of 1000%.
The number of explosions done by 108 Responsive Prayers in a single activation is increased by both

108 Responsive Prayers has a 0.5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.5 seconds by the same explosion. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.

With Limit Break, 108 Responsive Prayers can be further leveled up.

The name of this weapon may be a reference to the first entry in the Touhou Project bullet hell game series, Highly Responsive To Prayers. The weapon closely resembles ofuda amulets used by Shinto and Buddhist priests, including the game's protagonist, shrine maiden Reimu Hakurei.
